Definition: from G1909 and a presumed derivative of G2476; an appointee over, i.e. commander (teacher):--master.
BiblicalUsage: Epistates is Master — the title the disciples use for Jesus in Luke alone. Master, we have toiled all the night and have taken nothing; Master, Master, we perish; Master, it is good for us to be here; Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and the lepers lift up their voices, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
TheologicalSignificance: He is the one in charge of the boat, the mountain, and the mercy, and Master is the right name for Him. I believe the title says what the disciples knew, and what I am still learning: the boat is His, and so is the storm.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
